videos.title: The Crucible: 40 Golden Snooker Years
videos.description: Steve Davis goes back to the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield to celebrate 40 years of the Snooker World Championships. If the walls of this famous regional theatre could talk they would tell tales of tears, triumphs, laughter and top-class sport.

videos.title: Davis v Taylor: The '85 Black Ball Final
videos.description: A look back at the 1985 World Championship Snooker final. At its peak, over 18 and a half million people sat glued to their sets as Steve Davis and Dennis Taylor battled past midnight to a final and deciding black ball.

videos.title: To the Manor Born
videos.description: DeVere negotiates an important business deal with the beautiful Mademoiselle Dutoit, but when she decides to mix business with pleasure, he invents a wife... Audrey!

videos.title: Keeping Up Appearances
videos.description: When Hyacinth decides that a new car is in order, she aims rather higher than most people - much to Richard's horror.

videos.title: Anything Goes: The Musical
videos.description: When the SS American heads out to sea, etiquette and convention head out of the portholes as two unlikely pairs set off on the course to true love, proving that sometimes destiny needs a little help from a crew of singing sailors, a comical disguise and some good old-fashioned blackmail. Filmed live at the Barbican in London.

videos.title: South Pacific in London
videos.description: Follows the production of a new recording of `South Pacific', the classic musical that boasts many of the best and most enduring numbers written by Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein.

videos.title: The Truth About Christmas Carols
videos.description: There could be nothing sweeter and more sentimental than the sound of traditional carols performed by a velvet-voiced choir at Christmas, or so you would think. Composer Howard Goodall uncovers the surprising and often secret history of the Christmas carol. Far from being accepted as part of the celebrations of Jesus' birth, over the centuries carols have been banned by both church and state.

videos.title: Being the Brontës
videos.description: To mark the 200th anniversary of Charlotte Brontë's birth, Martha Kearney, novelist Helen Oyeyemi and journalist Lucy Mangan travel to Haworth Parsonage, the home of Charlotte and her sisters Emily and Anne, to discover the inspiration behind their classic novels `Jane Eyre', `Wuthering Heights' and `Agnes Grey'. The trio learn how the Brontës combined literary genius with real life experience to create some of the best-loved novels in the English language.

videos.title: Pompeii: The Mystery of the People Frozen in Time
videos.description: The city of Pompeii suffered a legendary volcanic disaster that left its citizens preserved in ashes. Yet no-one has been able to unravel the full story that is at the heart of our fascination: how did those bodies become frozen in time?

videos.title: This Green and Pleasant Land: The Story of British Landscape Painting
videos.description: Documentary which takes an eclectic group, including artists, critics and academics, into the countryside to look at how we have depicted our landscape in art, discovering how the genre carried British painting to its highest eminence and won a place in the nation's heart.

videos.title: Turner: The Man Who Painted Britain
videos.description: While Joseph Mallord William Turner is considered by many to be Britain's greatest landscape painter, his private life reveals a man of extremes and contradictions. This is a look at the extraordinary story of a brilliant self-made man.

videos.title: The Big Thinkers
videos.description: Lifespan is increasing by 2.5 years every decade, but living longer can come at a cost as old age brings with it a range of debilitating illnesses. Nobel laureate Sir Paul Nurse investigates the possibilities of a revolution in bio-medicine.
